product.title: The control plane for agentic software engineering
product.lede: Rotaris turns a high-level mission into coordinated work across planning, implementation, testing, documentation, Git, and verification. See what every agent is doing, intervene when necessary, and review the evidence before accepting the result.
product.closing: You get an inspectable software-engineering team — not one opaque coding agent.

orchestration.title: Orchestration
orchestration.body: Specialist agents — architect, coders, tester, verifier — coordinated as an engineering team.

control.title: Control
control.body: Inspect, pause, redirect, approve, or stop work at any point in the run.

verification.title: Verification
verification.body: Completion depends on requirements, tests, and explicit gates — not on an agent's say-so.

traceability.title: Traceability
traceability.body: Requirements, implementation, tests, agent actions, and artifacts remain connected.

define.title: Define the mission
define.body: Describe the change and its acceptance criteria. The requirements engineer turns them into persistent, numbered requirements.

plan.title: Review the plan
plan.body: The orchestrator decomposes the mission. Inspect tasks, dependencies, assigned agents, and models before anything runs.
plan.control: approve, edit, or reject the plan

delegate.title: Delegate to specialists
delegate.body: Work is routed to purpose-specific agents — analyst, architect, coding agents, tester, librarian — each with its own model and tools.

run.title: Run the team
run.body: Independent tasks execute concurrently; dependent work waits for its prerequisites. Iteration, depth, and fan-out limits bound every run.

control.title: Stay in control
control.body: Inspect any agent's transcript, tools, and context. Change configuration mid-run or respond to a failure with the recovery in view.

verify.title: Verify the result
verify.body: A verifier checks completed work against the requirements before the task is declared finished. Review the evidence, then accept.

views.title: Six views. One workspace.
views.lede: Everything the harness knows — sessions, agents, requirements, worktrees, artifacts, configuration — has one visible home.

overview.title: Overview
overview.body: Sessions, provider limits, token usage, and everything currently running — at a glance.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.body: The live transcript, the delegation tree, and the inspector — where you talk to the orchestrator.

mission.title: Mission
mission.body: The full task hierarchy: dependencies, per-agent models, tool counts, elapsed time, and state.

git.title: Git
git.body: Worktrees, branch context, changed files, diffs, and local commits made by agents — reviewable before anything leaves the machine.

library.title: Library
library.body: Requirements, agent reports, skills, and artifacts — the persistent knowledge a mission produces and consumes.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Providers, per-persona model routing, reasoning strength, MCP servers, and workspace security — dropdowns, not slash commands.

orchestration.title: A stable center. Specialists in motion.
orchestration.lede: Your orchestrator plans and delegates work to specialist agents. Independent tasks run in parallel; dependent tasks wait; every child reports back in a structured format the orchestrator can act on.

parallelism.body: Fan-out where tasks are independent, strict ordering where they are not.

bounded.body: Iteration limits, depth limits, fan-out limits, loop protection, and circuit breaking constrain every run.

reports.body: Each agent returns findings, changes, and evidence — not a wall of text.

cancellation.body: Stop a parent and every descendant stops with it — cleanly.

diagram.alt: Radial diagram: the orchestrator at the center — shown as a small net spanning delegation intensity per agent — delegating to seven specialist agents arranged in an even ring, each colored by state — done, running, or waiting

verification.title: Know why every change exists
verification.lede: Requirements and acceptance criteria are persistent engineering artifacts. Every change traces back to one — and forward to the test and verification that prove it.

chain.requirementBody: Session handlers shall be non-blocking under load.
chain.taskBody: Convert session handlers to async · coding-agent-1

gate.title: The verification gate
gate.body: Nothing is “done” because an agent said so. A dedicated verifier re-reads the requirements, re-runs the tests, and inspects the diff before a task is declared finished — and the completion summary shows you exactly what it found.
gate.traceability: Requirement-to-code and requirement-to-test links are enforced in the repository itself, so traceability survives long after the run.

band.note: No account required — download and point it at a repository.

control.title: Supervised autonomy, not blind trust
control.lede: Every agent's state, tools, elapsed time, context window, and model assignment stay visible while the run is live — and every consequential action has a human handle.

human.body: Pause a run, steer an agent mid-task, change its model or reasoning strength, or cancel — cancellation cascades to every descendant.

failure.body: Failures surface as states, not buried logs. The orchestrator re-delegates the fix with the failing evidence attached — and you can inspect or intervene at every step.

models.title: The right model for every role
models.lede: Route each persona to a different model by capability, cost, and availability. Set defaults at startup, override per run, and fall back automatically when a provider is unavailable.
models.overrides: Overrides apply per instance and take effect from the next iteration.
models.note: OAuth and API-key providers, local models, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Subscription limits are visible before you hit them.

security.title: Agents work inside the fence
security.lede: Every capability an agent has is scoped, logged, and revocable. Unsafe overrides exist — but they are explicit, and they are yours to grant.

files.title: Workspace-scoped file access
files.body: Agents read and write inside the selected workspace only, with path-traversal prevention.

shell.title: Controlled shell execution
shell.body: Shell commands run under workspace policy; consequential actions can require approval.

secrets.title: Secret redaction
secrets.body: Known secrets are redacted from transcripts, reports, and anything sent to a provider.

tokens.title: Restricted token storage
tokens.body: Provider credentials stay on your machine in ~/.local/share/rotaris/tokens/, in files readable only by your own user account (mode 0600).

loops.title: Loop protection
loops.body: Iteration limits and circuit breaking stop runaway agents before they burn tokens.

cancel.title: Cancellation, always
cancel.body: Any run, any agent, any time — cancellation propagates through the whole delegation tree.

where.local: The Rotaris application and orchestration engine run entirely on your machine. Your repository is never uploaded.
where.providers: Only the prompts and code context needed for a task are sent to the model providers you configure. With local models, nothing leaves the machine.
where.telemetry: No telemetry and no usage statistics. Sessions, logs, the response cache and the Git worktrees live in <0>.rotaris/</0> inside your workspace, configuration in <1>~/.config/rotaris/</1>. None of it reaches us.
where.update: The one connection Rotaris opens by itself is the start-up update check against GitHub, which tells GitHub your IP address and client details. Source installations never check, and an update installs only when the download matches the published SHA-256 checksum.

git.title: Isolated worktrees, reviewable commits
git.lede: Each session works in its own Git worktree, so parallel missions never trample each other. Agents commit locally with attributed authorship — you review diffs and decide what leaves the machine.

openSource.title: Built in the open
openSource.lede: MIT-licensed, CI-built from tagged commits, released with checksums. Every claim on this page maps to code you can read.
openSource.note: All releases are built by CI from tagged commits and published to GitHub Releases. Previous versions remain available for rollback and reproducibility.

what.a: A desktop application for running and supervising a team of specialized coding agents — an orchestration harness with a control plane, not a chat window with a single agent behind it.

python.a: No. The desktop application ships as a standalone build with the runtime bundled. Python is only needed for the optional CLI installation under Advanced installation.

code.q: Does my code leave my computer?
code.a: The application and engine run locally, and your repository is never uploaded. Prompts and the code context needed for a task are sent to the model providers you configure — with local models, nothing leaves the machine. The only connection Rotaris makes on its own is the start-up update check against GitHub.

providers.q: Which model providers can I use?
providers.a: OAuth providers such as GitHub Copilot, API-key providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI, local models, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Each persona can use a different model.

concurrency.a: Yes. Independent tasks run in parallel; dependent tasks wait for their prerequisites. Fan-out, depth, and iteration limits keep concurrency bounded.

finished.q: How does Rotaris decide a task is finished?
finished.a: A verifier checks the completed work against the mission's requirements and tests before the task is declared done. You review the completion summary and accept the result.

cancel.q: Can I pause or cancel a run?
cancel.a: At any time. Cancellation propagates through the delegation tree, so stopping a parent cleanly stops all of its descendants.

cli.a: Yes — a terminal interface is available for headless and scripted use, installed via pip. The desktop application is the primary product.

rename.a: It was renamed. Rotaris is the same orchestration engine and desktop application under its public name; the repository and the Python packages moved with it. Older links to geraet-ai still resolve.

security.q: How do I report a security issue?
security.a: Through the repository's security policy on GitHub — see the security section for the disclosure process and response expectations.

final.sub: Free, open source, no account required.
